This full-time role involves overall responsibility for the boutique’s commercial performance, client relationships, team development, and operational excellence. The manager will ensure that client interactions reflect luxury retail standards and that the boutique delivers both service and business results. Key Responsibilities Lead the achievement of sales, profitability, and productivity targets through business planning and performance monitoring. Build and strengthen a high-value client portfolio through strategic clienteling and relationship management. Recruit, lead, coach, and develop the boutique team, establishing clear expectations and a culture of service excellence. Ensure consistently elevated, personalized, and discreet service reflecting a distinguished jewellery house. Translate the House’s heritage and design identity into client experiences while upholding brand standards. Maintain visual presentation, product care, stock integrity, and operational discipline. Monitor sales performance, client activity, and other key indicators to identify opportunities. Develop an understanding of the Jeddah luxury market, client profiles, and competitive landscape. Collaborate with Retail Management, Marketing, Merchandising, and other teams to deliver commercial initiatives. 00752d38a5954cde.description: Our Purpose Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. Title And Summary Director, Strategic Partnerships & Partner Sales, Saudi Arabia Director, Strategic Partnerships & Partner Sales, Saudi Arabia Build Mastercard's partner-led growth engine in Saudi Arabia and turn strategic relationships into revenue. About The Role Saudi Arabia is one of the world's fastest-moving digital economies, and partnerships are central to how Mastercard will grow there. We are looking for an entrepreneurial, commercially driven leader to build and scale our partner-led business in the Kingdom and support opportunities across West Arabia. In this market-facing role, you will create new routes to market and design partnership propositions that bring Mastercard capabilities to new customers. You will be responsible for taking opportunities from the first executive conversation to signed business. You will work with a broad ecosystem that includes AI and digital platforms, cloud and cybersecurity providers, telecommunications companies, system integrators, fintechs, data businesses, and marketing and media organizations. What you will do Own growth: Lead the Saudi partner-sales strategy and deliver a revenue target through partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities. Create opportunities: Identify where Mastercard capabilities can be embedded, co-sold, or distributed through partner platforms and services. Focus areas include AI, cybersecurity, identity, fraud and financial crime, data insights, loyalty, and digital commerce. Shape propositions: Turn strategic discussions into clear use cases, target customers, and commercial models such as embedded, co-sell, reseller, referral, or joint-solution partnerships. Engage at senior levels: Build trusted relationships with founders, C-suite executives, and senior decision-makers across enterprise, technology, and government ecosystems. Drive execution: Lead joint business plans, account mapping, negotiations, and partner enablement to move opportunities from first engagement to first transaction. Collaborate across Mastercard: Work with product, sales, legal, finance, marketing, and delivery teams across the region and globally to bring partnerships to market. Scale what works: Turn successful use cases into repeatable commercial plays that can grow across Saudi Arabia and the wider region. What you will bring Extensive experience in strategic partnerships, partner sales, business development, platform sales, or enterprise technology. A proven record of originating and closing partner-led business while owning a commercial target. Strong knowledge of the Saudi market and an established network across technology, digital, telecommunications, financial services, government, data, or media ecosystems. Experience structuring partnerships and handling complex enterprise or government sales cycles. An entrepreneurial mindset. The role shapes the service model and operating concept across clinical care, rehabilitation, athlete health, performance, research and innovation, ensuring that the programme reflects QHC’s mandate, clinical standards and long-term strategic ambitions. The role leads the coordinated development of the sports medicine programme from concept through implementation. This includes service and facility design, technical and operational input to strategic partnerships and scopes of work, procurement requirements, workforce planning and hiring, technology and equipment requirements, governance, budgets and the key approvals required to establish integrated, athlete-centred and sustainable services. Working across executive, clinical and corporate leadership, the Director establishes priorities, integrates multidisciplinary workstreams and provides assurance on programme scope, quality, resources, risks, dependencies and delivery. Partnership Integration and Service Requirements • Define the clinical, operational, facility, workforce, technology and mobilisation requirements that sports medicine partners must address, and provide subject-matter input to the designated Sports Medicine Partnerships lead during partner assessment, selection and appointment. • Develop and validate the sports medicine technical and service requirements for scopes of work, requests for proposal, evaluation criteria, service levels, deliverables, acceptance measures, knowledge-transfer expectations and mobilisation plans, in coordination with the Partnerships, Commercial and Procurement functions. • Coordinate the operational integration of appointed partners into the sports medicine programme, ensuring that service interfaces, responsibilities, resources, data requirements, reporting, escalation routes and implementation dependencies are clearly defined. Work with Human Resources and clinical leaders to track deployment and mitigate critical workforce or capability gaps. 6. Implementation, Mobilisation and Service Activation • Direct the phased implementation and mobilisation of the sports medicine programme, translating approved designs and service plans into coordinated activation schedules, workstream deliverables, resource plans, acceptance criteria and transition requirements across clinical, operational and enabling functions. • Establish service-activation criteria and oversee multidisciplinary assurance activities, including document reviews, walkthroughs, simulations, workforce and system checks, partner readiness and regulatory confirmation. Provide evidence-based recommendations on phased activation, remediation or deferral based on safety, quality, capability and delivery risk. • Lead service activation and early operational stabilisation, coordinating issue resolution, escalation, executive reporting and corrective actions across QHC teams and appointed partners. Monitor initial performance against agreed safety, quality, workforce and service thresholds and transition stable services into business-as-usual governance. EXPERIENCE & ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS Advanced degree in Sports Medicine, Physiotherapy, Sports Science, Rehabilitation, Healthcare Management, or a related healthcare, clinical or performance discipline is preferred.
